title: CPR, AED, and the Chain of Survival

callouts.label: Scene Safety
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents scene safety.
callouts.ap_tip: Protect yourself and others. Move only when the scene itself is dangerous and training supports it.

callouts.label: Check Responsiveness
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents check responsiveness.
callouts.description: Tap and shout as taught to see whether the person responds.
callouts.ap_tip: Look for normal breathing. Gasping is not normal breathing.

callouts.label: Activate Emergency Response
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents activate emergency response.
callouts.description: Call emergency services or direct a specific person to call.
callouts.ap_tip: Use speakerphone when practical. Give the exact location.

callouts.label: Retrieve the AED
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents retrieve the aed.
callouts.description: Send someone to get an AED while help is activated.
callouts.ap_tip: AEDs are designed to guide users. Start care promptly rather than waiting beside the device location.

callouts.label: Hand Position
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents hand position.
callouts.description: Use the hand position taught in current certified training.
callouts.ap_tip: Technique varies with age and situation. Practice on a manikin, never forcefully on a classmate.

callouts.label: Chest Compressions
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents chest compressions.
callouts.description: High-quality compressions help circulate blood until advanced care arrives.
callouts.ap_tip: Follow current dispatcher or certified-training guidance for rate and depth. Allow full recoil and minimize interruptions.

callouts.label: Open the AED
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents open the aed.
callouts.description: Turn on or open the AED and follow its spoken and visual prompts.
callouts.ap_tip: Expose and prepare the chest as directed while preserving dignity. Do not improvise beyond training and device prompts.

callouts.label: Place Pads
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents place pads.
callouts.description: Place pads exactly as the diagrams on the pads show.
callouts.ap_tip: Pads need good contact with dry skin. Use pediatric equipment when directed and available.

callouts.label: Clear for Analysis
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents clear for analysis.
callouts.description: Make sure no one touches the person while the AED analyzes.
callouts.ap_tip: Say and visually check that everyone is clear. Motion can interfere with analysis.

callouts.label: Shock If Advised
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents shock if advised.
callouts.description: Deliver a shock only when the AED instructs it.
callouts.ap_tip: Confirm everyone is clear first. An AED will not advise every person to be shocked.

callouts.label: Resume CPR
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents resume cpr.
callouts.description: Resume compressions promptly after analysis or a shock as directed.
callouts.ap_tip: Continue following AED and dispatcher prompts. Switch compressors when trained help is available and fatigue affects quality.

callouts.label: Professional Handoff
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents professional handoff.
callouts.description: Continue until the person responds, the scene becomes unsafe, or trained responders take over.
callouts.ap_tip: Share what happened and what care was given. This poster is not a substitute for certified CPR/AED training.
